sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗，来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The horrible USAID.
sentences.zh: 这个可怕的美国国际开发署。

sentences.en: The horrible things that they're spending money on.
sentences.zh: 他们花钱的那些可怕项目。

sentences.en: It's got to be kickbacks, you know.
sentences.zh: 这肯定有回扣，你知道的。

sentences.en: As President Trump demolishes the government's biggest provider of foreign aid, the United States Agency for International Development, which he calls wasteful and misguided.
sentences.zh: 随着特朗普总统大举拆除政府最大的对外援助机构——美国国际开发署（他称该机构既浪费又被误导），

sentences.en: It's absolutely obscene.
sentences.zh: 这绝对令人发指。

sentences.en: Dangerous, bad, very costly.
sentences.zh: 危险、糟糕、代价高昂。

sentences.en: I mean, virtually every investment made is a cotton job.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，几乎每一笔投资都是骗局。

sentences.en: He's ending a 60-year bipartisan consensus about the best way to keep America safe from its enemies.
sentences.zh: 他正在终结一项长达60年、跨党派的共识，即如何保护美国免受敌人侵害的最佳方式。

sentences.en: Today, my colleagues, State Department reporter Michael Crowley and health reporter Stephanie Nolan on the rise and fall of USAID and American soft power.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事、国务院记者迈克尔·克劳利和健康记者斯蒂芬妮·诺兰将探讨美国国际开发署的兴衰及其软实力。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, February 11th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月11日，星期二。

sentences.en: Michael, as we speak to you, USAID has basically been dismantled.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，在我们采访你的时候，美国国际开发署基本上已经被拆解了。

sentences.en: A judge has paused elements of that dismantling, but the writing is very much on the wall.
sentences.zh: 法官已经暂停了拆解过程中的某些环节，但大局已定，覆水难收。

sentences.en: It's a shell of itself, so much so that its name has literally been removed from its headquarters in Washington.
sentences.zh: 它已经名存实亡，甚至连华盛顿总部的名字都被直接摘掉了。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of us have the sense that this elimination of this agency is a very big deal, even if we don't entirely understand exactly how USAID worked
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人都有这种感觉：取缔这个机构是一件大事，哪怕我们并不完全理解美国国际开发署的具体运作方式，

sentences.en: and why the United States was doing so much of this kind of foreign aid work on this scale to begin with.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么美国最初要在如此规模上开展这么多的这种对外援助工作。

sentences.en: So, what is that backstory?
sentences.zh: 那么，这背后的故事是什么？

sentences.en: Well, USAID was founded by President John F.
sentences.zh: 嗯，美国国际开发署是由约翰·F·总统创立的。

sentences.en: Kennedy, who created it with an executive order in 1961.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪在1961年通过一项行政命令创建了它。

sentences.en: And he did that not out of some pure sense of charity,
sentences.zh: 他这样做并非出于某种纯粹的慈善之心，

sentences.en: not out of a sense that there was famine in the world and America had a responsibility to address it.
sentences.zh: 也不是因为意识到世界上存在饥荒，美国负有解决它的责任。

sentences.en: The people who are opposed to aid should realize that this is a very powerful source of strength for us.
sentences.zh: 那些反对援助的人应该意识到，这是我们非常强大的力量源泉。

sentences.en: It was a matter of national security.
sentences.zh: 这是一个国家安全问题。

sentences.en: It permits us to exert influence for the maintenance of freedom.
sentences.zh: 它使我们能够施加影响力以维护自由。

sentences.en: He was reacting to the Cold War competition with the Soviet Union that was underway at the time.
sentences.zh: 他当时的反应是针对当时正在进行的与苏联的冷战竞争。

sentences.en: If we did not, we're not so heavily involved,
sentences.zh: 如果我们不这样做，没有这么深地介入，

sentences.en: our voice would not speak with such a vigor.
sentences.zh: 我们的声音就不会如此铿锵有力。

sentences.en: And which he saw as a real threat to America's primacy and security.
sentences.zh: 他认为这是对美国首要地位和安全的真正威胁。

sentences.en: And, you know, the Soviet Union was presenting itself as the champion, particularly in the developing world, of countries that had been under colonialism for decades or more
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，苏联把自己塑造成冠军，特别是在发展中国家，为那些遭受殖民统治几十甚至上百年、

sentences.en: and, you know, felt that they had been treated badly by the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 并且觉得受到西方虐待的国家发声。

sentences.en: And as we do not want to send American troops to a great many areas where freedom may be under attack, we send you.
sentences.zh: 既然我们不想把美军派往许多自由可能受到攻击的地区，我们就派你们去。

sentences.en: And Kennedy felt like America had to show that we are not exploiting the world around us.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪觉得美国必须表明我们没有剥削我们周围的世界。

sentences.en: We care about its welfare.
sentences.zh: 我们关心它的福祉。

sentences.en: Working with the people in those countries to try to work with them in developing the economic thrust of their country so that they can make a determination
sentences.zh: 与这些国家的人民合作，试图与他们合作发展其国家的经济实力，以便他们能够做出决定，

sentences.en: that they can solve their problems without resorting to totalitarian control and becoming part of the bloc.
sentences.zh: 即他们能够解决自己的问题，而无需诉诸极权统治并成为集团的一部分。

sentences.en: And ultimately, this is the most important part, choose us and not the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，最重要的一点是，选择我们而不是苏联。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Choose democracy and capitalism, not communism.
sentences.zh: 选择民主和资本主义，而不是共产主义。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And in Kennedy's mind, the United States had a real problem.
sentences.zh: 在肯尼迪看来，美国面临着一个真正的问题。

sentences.en: The United States was at risk of losing this competition with the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 美国面临着在这场与苏联的竞争中落败的风险。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, one thing that motivated Kennedy, and it's such an interesting footnote to all of this, was a popular best-selling book at the time called The Ugly American.
sentences.zh: 嗯，促使肯尼迪的一个因素——这也是这一切中一个非常有趣的注脚——是当时一本畅销书，名叫《丑陋的美国人》。

sentences.en: The Ugly American essentially told the story that American diplomats in Asia were out of touch with the places where they were working.
sentences.zh: 《丑陋的美国人》基本上讲述了这样一个故事：亚洲的美国外交官与他们工作的地方脱节。

sentences.en: They didn't understand the local culture.
sentences.zh: 他们不了解当地文化。

sentences.en: They seemed like they had parachuted in from another world and, in some cases, made more enemies than friends.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来像是从另一个世界空降来的，在某些情况下，树敌多于交友。

sentences.en: And this was a big problem for the United States, that Americans were seen as ugly.
sentences.zh: 这对美国来说是个大问题，美国人被视为丑陋的。

sentences.en: And Kennedy actually recommended that his associates and members of Congress read this book to understand this problem.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪甚至建议他的同僚和国会议员阅读这本书，以了解这个问题。

sentences.en: And he felt like America had to stop presenting the ugly face and had to present a more benevolent, helpful face.
sentences.zh: 他觉得美国必须停止呈现丑陋的面孔，而必须呈现一个更加仁慈、更有帮助的面孔。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: So USAID, in Kennedy's mind, is the antidote to the perception of the ugly American.
sentences.zh: 所以在肯尼迪看来，美国国际开发署是对“丑陋美国人”形象的解药。

sentences.en: It is the generous American, the altruistic American, who shows up strategically with humanitarian aid and makes your life, if you're overseas,
sentences.zh: 它是慷慨的美国人，是无私的美国人，带着人道主义援助战略性地出现，如果你身处海外且对美国持怀疑态度，

sentences.en: skeptical of America, materially better.
sentences.zh: 它能让你的生活在物质上变得更好。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: USAID is building schools, building hospitals, providing people with clean drinking water, life-saving medicines, helping them find employment, developing local infrastructure,
sentences.zh: 美国国际开发署在修建学校、修建医院、为人们提供清洁饮用水、救命药物、帮助他们寻找就业机会、发展当地基础设施，

sentences.en: all kinds of things that help people in a fundamental day-to-day way have better lives in these countries.
sentences.zh: 以及所有这些以基本的日常方式帮助这些国家的人民过上更好生活的各种事情。

sentences.en: But part of what's happening as USAID does this work is you're gaining influence, you're getting to know government officials,
sentences.zh: 但美国国际开发署在做这项工作时发生的一部分事情是，你正在获得影响力，你正在结识政府官员，

sentences.en: you're getting to know people in the local population.
sentences.zh: 你正在结识当地民众。

sentences.en: So this kind of becomes the basis of what we know as soft power, which is distinct from hard power.
sentences.zh: 所以这在某种程度上成为了我们所知的软实力的基础，软实力不同于硬实力。

sentences.en: That's military power.
sentences.zh: 那是军事力量。

sentences.en: Soft power is influence in relationships.
sentences.zh: 软实力是影响力和人际关系。

sentences.en: And a bipartisan consensus forms around the value of soft power as an instrument of American foreign policy going forward for decades.
sentences.zh: 并且围绕着软实力作为几十年后美国外交政策工具的价值，形成了一种跨党派的共识。

sentences.en: And so Kennedy launches USAID, but year after year, presidents of both parties accept USAID as a central part of American foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 因此，肯尼迪创立了美国国际开发署，但年复一年，两党总统都接受美国国际开发署作为美国外交政策的核心部分。

sentences.en: I have to imagine, however, that when the U.S.
sentences.zh: 然而，我不得不想象，当美国在20世纪80年代末、90年代初赢得冷战时，

sentences.en: wins the Cold War by the end of the 1980s, the early 1990s, that this poses something of a challenge to USAID's purpose.
sentences.zh: 这给美国国际开发署的宗旨带来了一些挑战。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But at the same time, some pretty good new rationales emerge for the continuation of a robust USAID.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，一些非常好的新理由也应运而生，以继续保持一个强有力的美国国际开发署。

sentences.en: USAID.
sentences.zh: 美国国际开发署。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because after 9-11,
sentences.zh: 因为9·11之后，

sentences.en: America realized that the Soviet communist ideology that threatened us had been replaced by a new ideology.
sentences.zh: 美国意识到威胁我们的苏联共产主义意识形态已经被一种新意识形态所取代。

sentences.en: It was a terrorist ideology.
sentences.zh: 这是一种恐怖主义意识形态。

sentences.en: It was a radical fundamentalism that was emerging from parts of the world where USAID did a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 这是一种激进的原教旨主义，从美国国际开发署开展了大量工作的世界某些地区涌现出来。

sentences.en: And that terrorism really flourished in countries where there was instability, weak civil society.
sentences.zh: 而这种恐怖主义确实在动荡、公民社会薄弱的国家滋生。

sentences.en: You know, when a state collapses entirely, that becomes a breeding ground for radicalism.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当一个国家彻底崩溃时，这就成了激进主义的温床。

sentences.en: And so there was a new value placed on American aid programs in countries that could maintain stability, try to help find jobs for people who might otherwise turn to radicalism,
sentences.zh: 因此，人们对在能够维持稳定的国家开展的美国援助项目赋予了新的价值，试图帮助那些本可能转向激进主义的人找到工作，

sentences.en: all kinds of programs that were perceived as being part of the mission of combating worldwide terrorism.
sentences.zh: 以及被视为打击全球恐怖主义使命一部分的各种项目。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it's also during that period that we see some of USAID's real limitations and, frankly, some of the most wasteful projects that it's ever undertaken.
sentences.zh: 但正是在这段时期，我们也看到了美国国际开发署的一些真正局限性，坦率地说，还有它所开展的一些最浪费的项目。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: Well, there was one project in Afghanistan known as Promote that was meant to empower women in the country, give them workplace experience.
sentences.zh: 嗯，阿富汗有一个名为“促进”（Promote）的项目，旨在赋予该国女性权力，赐予她们职场经验。

sentences.en: It was originally budgeted at $280 million, and it was supposed to help 75,000 women get jobs, promotions, apprenticeships, internships.
sentences.zh: 它最初的预算为2.8亿美元，本应帮助75,000名女性获得工作、晋升、学徒和实习机会。

sentences.en: But an inspector general report that came out a few years ago found that only 55 women had been promoted to better jobs.
sentences.zh: 但几年前发布的一份监察长报告发现，只有55名女性晋升到了更好的工作岗位。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Out of 75,000, original goal.
sentences.zh: 在最初设定的75,000人目标中。

sentences.en: That was the original goal.
sentences.zh: 那是最初的目标。

sentences.en: And the inspector general essentially said the whole thing had been a complete waste.
sentences.zh: 监察长基本上表示，整个项目完全是一场彻底的浪费。

sentences.en: So basically, a nearly $300 million program funded by us, the taxpayer, turned out to have been a boondoggle.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，由我们纳税人资助的近3亿美元的项目，结果变成了一场毫无价值的失败投资。

sentences.en: Yeah, basically down the tubes.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上打了水漂。

sentences.en: So, look, you might cut them some slack for having been in a war zone.
sentences.zh: 所以，看在他们身处战区的份上，你或许可以对他们网开一面。

sentences.en: A lot of projects were tried by a lot of different parts of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国政府在伊拉克和阿富汗的许多不同部门尝试了许多项目，结果都泡汤了。

sentences.en: government in Iraq and Afghanistan that just flopped.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Even granting that,
sentences.zh: 即便承认这一点，

sentences.en: USAID has maintained strong bipartisan support for years and years.
sentences.zh: 美国国际开发署多年来一直保持着强烈的跨党派支持。

sentences.en: And the view of both parties is that not every project is going to work perfectly.
sentences.zh: 两党的观点是，并非每个项目都会完美运行。

sentences.en: Not every dollar is going to give you an ideal return.
sentences.zh: 并非每一美元都会给你带来理想的回报。

sentences.en: But that at the end of the day, relative to the national budget,
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，相对于国家预算而言，

sentences.en: USAID does not spend that much money.
sentences.zh: 美国国际开发署并没有花那么多钱。

sentences.en: And actually, overall, you get a good return on your dollar.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，总体而言，你物有所值。

sentences.en: And you're getting real value for American interests.
sentences.zh: 你为美国的利益获得了真正的价值。

sentences.en: And that USAID is important to continue in support.
sentences.zh: 而且美国国际开发署对于继续给予支持非常重要。

sentences.en: That it's really good for the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 这对美利坚合众国真的很好。

sentences.en: Perhaps the clearest example of how USAID exerts American soft power is through the work it's done in public health.
sentences.zh: 或许，美国国际开发署如何发挥美国软实力最明显的例子，就是它在公共卫生领域所做的工作。

sentences.en: And to understand that, I spoke with my colleague, global health reporter,
sentences.zh: 为了理解这一点，我采访了我的同事、全球健康记者

sentences.en: Stephanie Nolan.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬妮·诺兰。

sentences.en: Stephanie, how big a part of USAID's budget and work is healthcare, the subject you have spent so much of your career covering?
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬妮，医疗卫生——这个你大半个职业生涯都在报道的主题——在美援署的预算和工作中占了多大的比重？

sentences.en: So it's roughly a third.
sentences.zh: 大约占三分之一。

sentences.en: If you think about USAID having a budget of about $40 billion, about $12.5 billion of that was spent on healthcare.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑到美国国际开发署的预算约为400亿美元，其中大约125亿美元用于医疗卫生。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it's a really meaningful part of what this agency does around the world.
sentences.zh: 所以这是该机构在全球范围内所做工作的一个非常重要的部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: And in your global travels, which are many and varied, how frequently do you encounter a USAID program of one kind or another?
sentences.zh: 在你丰富多样的全球旅行中，你遇到这样或那样的美国国际开发署项目的频率有多高？

sentences.en: I would have to think for a long time to think of a trip when I have not come across either U.S.-funded research or medications or humanitarian assistance.
sentences.zh: 我得仔细想想，有哪些旅行是我没有遇到美国资助的研究、药物或人道主义援助的。

sentences.en: And one of the big ones is the HIV program, which was started at the height of, you know, if you think back 20 years to when there were almost 30 million people living with HIV
sentences.zh: 其中最大的一项是艾滋病项目，它启动于艾滋病盛行的时期，你知道的，如果你回想20年前，撒哈拉以南非洲有近3000万人携带艾滋病毒，

sentences.en: in sub-Saharan Africa and no treatment and people were dying in just these extraordinary numbers.
sentences.zh: 当时没有治疗方法，人们正以惊人的数字死亡。

sentences.en: And at that point,
sentences.zh: 就在那时，

sentences.en: President George W.
sentences.zh: 乔治·W·总统

sentences.en: Bush created this emergency AIDS response program and it has brought life-saving HIV medication to millions and millions of people.
sentences.zh: 布什创建了这一紧急艾滋病应对计划，它为数百万乃至数千万人带来了拯救生命的艾滋病毒药物。

sentences.en: Today, there's about 21 million people who rely on that program for that medication.
sentences.zh: 如今，大约有2100万人依靠该项目获得这些药物。

sentences.en: It's been responsible for getting drugs to hundreds of thousands of women with HIV who were giving birth to make sure that their babies weren't infected.
